paragraphs.title: The Waters Recede and the Ark Rests

easy.question: Whom did God remember at the beginning of this passage?
answers: Noah and the animals
The people of the city
The king of Egypt
easy.explanation: The verse says that God remembered Noah and every living thing and all the cattle with him in the ark.

easy.question: What happened to the waters after God caused a wind to pass over the earth?
answers: They began to rise
They subsided and began to decrease
They froze
easy.explanation: The verse says that the wind caused the waters to subside, meaning that they calmed and decreased.

easy.question: Where did the ark rest?
answers: On Mount Carmel
On Mount Sinai
On the mountains of Ararat
easy.explanation: Verse 4 says that the ark rested on the mountains of Ararat.

medium.question: What happened after the fountains of the deep were stopped and the rain ceased?
answers: The waters began to recede and decrease
The ark sank
The rain grew stronger
medium.explanation: After the sources of water were stopped, the waters gradually receded from the earth.

medium.question: What does the phrase “the rain from heaven was restrained” mean in this context?
answers: It became stronger
It stopped
It began to fall
medium.explanation: The context shows that the rain ceased to fall, so it was stopped or restrained.

medium.question: Which event happened first?
answers: The tops of the mountains were seen
The waters disappeared completely
The ark rested on the mountains of Ararat
medium.explanation: The ark rested in the seventh month, while the tops of the mountains were not seen until the tenth month.

challenge.question: What does the sequence of events show about the meaning of “God remembered Noah”?
answers: God acted for Noah’s benefit, and the wind caused the waters to subside
Noah had forgotten God
God merely thought of Noah’s name without doing anything
challenge.explanation: Immediately afterward, the passage describes God’s action: He caused a wind to pass over the earth, and the waters subsided.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “upon the mountains of Ararat”?
answers: The ark rested inside the city of Ararat
The ark rested in a mountainous region called Ararat
The ark rested on one mountain named Ararat
challenge.explanation: The word “mountains” is plural, so the phrase refers to a mountainous region rather than necessarily one mountain.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the fact that the ark had already rested, but the mountain tops were seen only later?
answers: The ark rested before the Flood began
The mountains disappeared after the ark rested
The waters continued to decrease after the ark rested
challenge.explanation: The passage first mentions the ark resting and later the mountain tops becoming visible, showing that the waters continued to recede.

questions.question: What does the sequence of events show about the meaning of “God remembered Noah”?
answers: God acted for Noah’s benefit, and the wind caused the waters to subside
Noah had forgotten God
God merely thought of Noah’s name without doing anything
questions.explanation: Immediately afterward, the passage describes God’s action: He caused a wind to pass over the earth, and the waters subsided.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “upon the mountains of Ararat”?
answers: The ark rested inside the city of Ararat
The ark rested in a mountainous region called Ararat
The ark rested on one mountain named Ararat
questions.explanation: The word “mountains” is plural, so the phrase refers to a mountainous region rather than necessarily one mountain.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the fact that the ark had already rested, but the mountain tops were seen only later?
answers: The ark rested before the Flood began
The mountains disappeared after the ark rested
The waters continued to decrease after the ark rested
questions.explanation: The passage first mentions the ark resting and later the mountain tops becoming visible, showing that the waters continued to recede.

paragraphs.title: Noah Sends Out the Raven and the Dove

easy.question: What did Noah do at the end of forty days?
answers: He opened the window of the ark
He left the ark
He sent out the dove
easy.explanation: After forty days, Noah opened the window of the ark.

easy.question: Which bird did Noah send out first?
answers: The dove
The raven
The eagle
easy.explanation: The passage says that Noah first sent out the raven.

easy.question: Why did the dove return to Noah?
answers: It was afraid of the raven
Noah called it
It found no place to rest its foot
easy.explanation: The dove returned because the waters still covered the earth and it found no place to rest.

medium.question: What was the order of Noah’s actions after he opened the ark’s window?
answers: He sent out the dove and then the raven
He sent out the raven and then the dove
He immediately left the ark
medium.explanation: Noah first sent out the raven and afterward sent out the dove to test the condition of the waters.

medium.question: What does “no rest for the sole of her foot” mean in this context?
answers: A place to rest or stand
Food for the bird
An opening in the ark
medium.explanation: The phrase means that the dove found no place outside the ark where it could rest its foot.

medium.question: Why did Noah send out the dove after sending out the raven?
answers: To bring food into the ark
To see whether the waters had decreased from the earth
To find the raven
medium.explanation: Noah sent out the dove to see whether the waters had gone down from the surface of the ground.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the fact that the dove returned to Noah and that he took it by the hand?
answers: The dove found dry land outside the ark
The dove could not find a place to rest outside the ark
The dove refused to leave the ark
challenge.explanation: The dove returned because it found no place to rest, and Noah brought it back into the ark.

challenge.question: What difference does the passage describe between the raven and the dove?
answers: The raven went back and forth, while the dove returned to Noah
The raven stayed in the ark, while the dove did not leave
The raven found a resting place, while the dove brought a branch
challenge.explanation: The raven went “to and fro,” while the dove went out, found no rest, and returned to Noah.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “he put forth his hand, and took her” show about Noah’s action?
answers: Noah closed the ark’s window
Noah threw the dove into the water
Noah helped the dove back into the ark
challenge.explanation: When the dove returned, Noah reached out, took it, and pulled it back into the ark.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the fact that the dove returned to Noah and that he took it by the hand?
answers: The dove found dry land outside the ark
The dove could not find a place to rest outside the ark
The dove refused to leave the ark
questions.explanation: The dove returned because it found no place to rest, and Noah brought it back into the ark.

questions.question: What difference does the passage describe between the raven and the dove?
answers: The raven went back and forth, while the dove returned to Noah
The raven stayed in the ark, while the dove did not leave
The raven found a resting place, while the dove brought a branch
questions.explanation: The raven went “to and fro,” while the dove went out, found no rest, and returned to Noah.

questions.question: What does the phrase “he put forth his hand, and took her” show about Noah’s action?
answers: Noah closed the ark’s window
Noah threw the dove into the water
Noah helped the dove back into the ark
questions.explanation: When the dove returned, Noah reached out, took it, and pulled it back into the ark.

paragraphs.title: The Dove Brings an Olive Leaf

easy.question: Which bird did Noah send out from the ark?
answers: The dove
The raven
The eagle
easy.explanation: The passage says that Noah sent the dove out from the ark.

easy.question: How many more days did Noah wait before sending the dove out again?
answers: Three days
Seven days
Forty days
easy.explanation: The passage says that he stayed yet another seven days.

easy.question: What did the dove carry in its mouth?
answers: A fig branch
A stone
An olive leaf
easy.explanation: The dove returned to Noah with an olive leaf in its mouth.

medium.question: How did Noah know that the waters had decreased from the earth?
answers: The dove brought an olive leaf
The dove did not leave the ark
Noah saw the mountains
medium.explanation: The olive leaf showed that vegetation had emerged from the waters, so Noah knew that the waters had gone down.

medium.question: What does the phrase “an olive leaf pluckt off” mean?
answers: A leaf that had been eaten
A leaf picked or torn from a tree
A very large leaf
medium.explanation: The phrase describes a leaf that had been plucked or picked from an olive tree.

medium.question: What sequence of events is described in the passage?
answers: The dove did not return, then brought a leaf, and was sent out last
Noah saw the mountains, then sent out a raven, and finally the waters decreased
Noah waited seven days, the dove returned with a leaf, and after seven more days it did not return
medium.explanation: First Noah waited seven days and sent out the dove; it returned with an olive leaf, and after another seven days it did not return.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the fact that the dove did not return to Noah the last time?
answers: The dove found a place to rest outside the ark, suggesting that the land was becoming more suitable for leaving
The dove disappeared inside the ark
The waters began to rise again
challenge.explanation: Since the dove did not return, it likely found a suitable place outside the ark, consistent with the continued decrease of the waters.

challenge.question: What do the words “yet” and “other” emphasize in the passage?
answers: That Noah stopped waiting
That additional periods of waiting and sending followed what had already happened
That the dove was sent only once
challenge.explanation: These words show continuation: Noah waited additional days and sent the dove again after an earlier sending.

challenge.question: What is the more precise conclusion after the dove returned with an olive leaf?
answers: The whole earth was already completely dry
Noah immediately left the ark
The waters had decreased, but the passage does not yet say that the whole earth was dry
challenge.explanation: Noah knew only that the waters had decreased from the earth; the passage does not say that the entire earth was already dry.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the fact that the dove did not return to Noah the last time?
answers: The dove found a place to rest outside the ark, suggesting that the land was becoming more suitable for leaving
The dove disappeared inside the ark
The waters began to rise again
questions.explanation: Since the dove did not return, it likely found a suitable place outside the ark, consistent with the continued decrease of the waters.

questions.question: What do the words “yet” and “other” emphasize in the passage?
answers: That Noah stopped waiting
That additional periods of waiting and sending followed what had already happened
That the dove was sent only once
questions.explanation: These words show continuation: Noah waited additional days and sent the dove again after an earlier sending.

questions.question: What is the more precise conclusion after the dove returned with an olive leaf?
answers: The whole earth was already completely dry
Noah immediately left the ark
The waters had decreased, but the passage does not yet say that the whole earth was dry
questions.explanation: Noah knew only that the waters had decreased from the earth; the passage does not say that the entire earth was already dry.

easy.question: Who removed the covering of the ark?
answers: Noah
Moses
Abraham
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Noah removed the covering of the ark.”

easy.question: What did Noah see after removing the ark’s covering?
answers: That the rain had begun
That the face of the ground was dry
That the animals had left
easy.explanation: Noah saw that the face of the ground was dry.

easy.question: When was the earth completely dry according to the passage?
answers: On the first day of the first month
On the seventh day
On the twenty-seventh day of the second month
easy.explanation: The passage says that the earth was dry on the twenty-seventh day of the second month.

medium.question: What is the correct order of events in the passage?
answers: The earth became completely dry, and then Noah removed the covering
Noah left the ark, and then the waters dried up
The waters dried up, Noah removed the covering, and afterward the earth was dry
medium.explanation: First the waters dried up from the earth, then Noah removed the covering, and finally the passage says that the earth was dry.

medium.question: What does “the covering of the ark” refer to?
answers: The water surrounding the ark
The ark’s cover
The ark’s door
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the cover or upper covering of the ark, which Noah removed to look outside.

medium.question: What can be understood from Noah removing the covering and then looking?
answers: He wanted to check the condition of the earth
He wanted to add water to the ark
He wanted to build a new ark
medium.explanation: Noah removed the covering and saw that the face of the ground was dry, showing that he was checking the condition of the earth.

challenge.question: What important difference appears between the beginning and the end of the passage?
answers: At first Noah went out, and at the end he went in
At first it rained, and at the end the Flood began
At first the face of the ground was dry, and at the end the whole earth was dry
challenge.explanation: The beginning describes the drying of the ground’s surface, while the end says that the earth was dry, showing progress in the drying process.

challenge.question: Why can we not say that the whole earth was already dry on the first day of the first month?
answers: At that time the passage says only that the face of the ground was dry
Noah was not yet in the ark
The Flood began on that day
challenge.explanation: The first verse speaks only of the “face of the ground,” while the earth is explicitly said to be dry only later.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the gap between the two dates?
answers: The waters returned to cover the earth
The drying process took time and did not finish immediately
Noah forgot when the Flood began
challenge.explanation: The first date describes partial drying, while the later date describes the drying of the earth; therefore, the process continued over time.

questions.question: What important difference appears between the beginning and the end of the passage?
answers: At first Noah went out, and at the end he went in
At first it rained, and at the end the Flood began
At first the face of the ground was dry, and at the end the whole earth was dry
questions.explanation: The beginning describes the drying of the ground’s surface, while the end says that the earth was dry, showing progress in the drying process.

questions.question: Why can we not say that the whole earth was already dry on the first day of the first month?
answers: At that time the passage says only that the face of the ground was dry
Noah was not yet in the ark
The Flood began on that day
questions.explanation: The first verse speaks only of the “face of the ground,” while the earth is explicitly said to be dry only later.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the gap between the two dates?
answers: The waters returned to cover the earth
The drying process took time and did not finish immediately
Noah forgot when the Flood began
questions.explanation: The first date describes partial drying, while the later date describes the drying of the earth; therefore, the process continued over time.

paragraphs.title: The Command to Leave the Ark

easy.question: To whom did God speak in verse 15?
answers: Noah
Abraham
Moses
easy.explanation: The verse explicitly says, “God spake unto Noah.”

easy.question: What did God command Noah to do?
answers: Build an ark
Leave the ark
Enter the ark
easy.explanation: God commanded Noah, “Go forth of the ark.”

easy.question: Who left the ark with Noah?
answers: Only his sons
Only his wife
His wife, his sons, and his sons’ wives
easy.explanation: The passage says that Noah left with his wife, his sons, and his sons’ wives.

medium.question: What order of events is described in the passage?
answers: God speaks to Noah, Noah and his family leave, and the animals leave
The animals leave, God speaks, and then Noah enters
Noah builds the ark, and then God speaks to him
medium.explanation: First God speaks to Noah, then commands him and his family to leave, and finally commands him to bring out the animals as well.

medium.question: What is expected to happen after the animals leave the ark?
answers: They will immediately return to the ark
They will breed abundantly and fill the earth
They will all remain in one place
medium.explanation: The passage says that they will breed abundantly and be fruitful and multiply upon the earth.

medium.question: What does “that they may breed abundantly in the earth” mean?
answers: They will rest on the earth
They will flee from the earth
They will reproduce and spread throughout the earth
medium.explanation: The context includes being fruitful and multiplying, so the phrase means that the animals will reproduce and spread throughout the earth.

challenge.question: What central idea emerges from the command for Noah, his family, and the animals to leave the ark?
answers: A renewed beginning of life on the earth
A continuation of life inside the ark
A separation between Noah and the animals
challenge.explanation: Leaving the ark and multiplying mark a renewed beginning of life on the earth.

challenge.question: Why was Noah told “Go forth” even though the command also included his wife, sons, and sons’ wives?
answers: Because Noah alone was in the ark
Because Noah was the leader to whom the command was addressed
Because his family was not allowed to leave
challenge.explanation: The command is addressed to Noah, but it explicitly includes the members of his family who were with him in the ark.

challenge.question: What can be learned from the listing of birds, cattle, and creeping things?
answers: Only flying animals were saved
The animals were meant to remain in the ark
The command to continue life applied to many kinds of animals
challenge.explanation: The passage names birds, cattle, and creeping things to show that leaving and multiplying involved many kinds of animals.

questions.question: What central idea emerges from the command for Noah, his family, and the animals to leave the ark?
answers: A renewed beginning of life on the earth
A continuation of life inside the ark
A separation between Noah and the animals
questions.explanation: Leaving the ark and multiplying mark a renewed beginning of life on the earth.

questions.question: Why was Noah told “Go forth” even though the command also included his wife, sons, and sons’ wives?
answers: Because Noah alone was in the ark
Because Noah was the leader to whom the command was addressed
Because his family was not allowed to leave
questions.explanation: The command is addressed to Noah, but it explicitly includes the members of his family who were with him in the ark.

questions.question: What can be learned from the listing of birds, cattle, and creeping things?
answers: Only flying animals were saved
The animals were meant to remain in the ark
The command to continue life applied to many kinds of animals
questions.explanation: The passage names birds, cattle, and creeping things to show that leaving and multiplying involved many kinds of animals.

easy.question: Who left the ark together with Noah?
answers: His family
Only the animals
The people of the city
easy.explanation: Noah left the ark with his sons, his wife, and his sons’ wives.

easy.question: From where did the animals leave?
answers: From the mountain
From the ark
From the city
easy.explanation: The passage says that all the animals left the ark.

easy.question: Which animals are mentioned among those leaving the ark?
answers: Only fish
Only birds
Beasts, creeping things, and birds
easy.explanation: The passage mentions every beast, every creeping thing, and every fowl.

medium.question: What can be understood from the fact that Noah and his family left together?
answers: They left as one family
Only Noah was permitted to leave
The family remained in the ark
medium.explanation: The passage lists the members of Noah’s family and emphasizes that they all left with him.

medium.question: What does “every creeping thing upon the earth” refer to?
answers: Creatures that fly in the sky
Creatures that move or crawl on the ground
Creatures that live in the water
medium.explanation: The words “upon the earth” show that these are creatures that move or crawl across the ground.

medium.question: What was the general order of events described in the passage?
answers: The animals left, and then Noah entered
Noah and his family left, followed by the animals
Everyone remained in the ark
medium.explanation: Verse 18 describes Noah and his family leaving, and verse 19 describes the animals leaving.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “after their kinds” show about the animals’ departure?
answers: They left in groups or according to their kinds
They left only with human family members
They left without any order
challenge.explanation: The phrase indicates that the animals left according to their kinds, or groups.

challenge.question: Why does the passage repeat the word “every” in describing the animals?
answers: To say that only a few species left
To emphasize that all kinds of animals were included
To distinguish Noah from his sons
challenge.explanation: The repeated word emphasizes that the departure from the ark included the animals broadly.

challenge.question: What wording is shared by Noah and the animals in the description of their departure?
answers: Both are said to leave the ark
Both remained inside the ark
Both built the ark
challenge.explanation: Noah and his family are said to go forth, and the animals are said to go forth out of the ark; all of them left it.

questions.question: What does the phrase “after their kinds” show about the animals’ departure?
answers: They left in groups or according to their kinds
They left only with human family members
They left without any order
questions.explanation: The phrase indicates that the animals left according to their kinds, or groups.

questions.question: Why does the passage repeat the word “every” in describing the animals?
answers: To say that only a few species left
To emphasize that all kinds of animals were included
To distinguish Noah from his sons
questions.explanation: The repeated word emphasizes that the departure from the ark included the animals broadly.

questions.question: What wording is shared by Noah and the animals in the description of their departure?
answers: Both are said to leave the ark
Both remained inside the ark
Both built the ark
questions.explanation: Noah and his family are said to go forth, and the animals are said to go forth out of the ark; all of them left it.

paragraphs.title: Noah Builds an Altar and Offers Sacrifices

easy.question: Who built an altar to the Lord?
answers: Noah
Abraham
Moses
easy.explanation: The verse explicitly says, “Noah builded an altar unto the Lord.”

easy.question: For whom did Noah build the altar?
answers: For his family
For the Lord
For the animals
easy.explanation: Noah built the altar for the Lord, as the verse says.

easy.question: What did Noah offer on the altar?
answers: Water
Bread
Burnt offerings
easy.explanation: The passage says that Noah offered burnt offerings on the altar.

medium.question: What did Noah do in the order described in the verse?
answers: He built an altar, took clean animals and birds, and offered burnt offerings
He offered burnt offerings, built an altar, and then took birds
He took all the animals, built a house, and offered water
medium.explanation: The verse presents this order: building the altar, taking clean animals and birds, and offering burnt offerings.

medium.question: What does “burnt offerings” mean in this context?
answers: Steps
Sacrifices burned on the altar
Special garments
medium.explanation: Burnt offerings were sacrifices placed on the altar and burned.

medium.question: Which animals did Noah take for the burnt offerings?
answers: Every animal without exception
Only fish
Clean cattle and clean birds
medium.explanation: The verse emphasizes that Noah took from every clean beast and every clean fowl.

challenge.question: Which detail shows that Noah chose the animals carefully?
answers: The emphasis on clean beasts and clean birds
The mention of building the altar
The word “Noah”
challenge.explanation: The repeated emphasis on clean animals shows that they were selected deliberately rather than taken at random.

challenge.question: Why can we say that Noah’s offering included both cattle and birds?
answers: Because the word “altar” includes both
Because the verse separately mentions clean beasts and clean birds
Because all animals go up on the altar
challenge.explanation: The verse names two distinct groups: clean beasts and clean birds.

challenge.question: What does the transition from building the altar to offering burnt offerings show about the altar’s purpose?
answers: It was meant to be a dwelling place
It was meant to gather the animals
It served for worship of the Lord and the offering of sacrifices
challenge.explanation: Immediately after building the altar, Noah offered burnt offerings on it to the Lord, showing its purpose.

questions.question: Which detail shows that Noah chose the animals carefully?
answers: The emphasis on clean beasts and clean birds
The mention of building the altar
The word “Noah”
questions.explanation: The repeated emphasis on clean animals shows that they were selected deliberately rather than taken at random.

questions.question: Why can we say that Noah’s offering included both cattle and birds?
answers: Because the word “altar” includes both
Because the verse separately mentions clean beasts and clean birds
Because all animals go up on the altar
questions.explanation: The verse names two distinct groups: clean beasts and clean birds.

questions.question: What does the transition from building the altar to offering burnt offerings show about the altar’s purpose?
answers: It was meant to be a dwelling place
It was meant to gather the animals
It served for worship of the Lord and the offering of sacrifices
questions.explanation: Immediately after building the altar, Noah offered burnt offerings on it to the Lord, showing its purpose.

paragraphs.title: The Promise of the Natural Cycles

easy.question: What kind of smell did the Lord smell?
answers: A sweet savor
The smell of rain
The smell of the earth
easy.explanation: The verse says that the Lord smelled a sweet savor.

easy.question: What did the Lord say He would no longer do to every living thing?
answers: He would no longer send rain
He would no longer strike every living thing
He would no longer create animals
easy.explanation: The Lord said that He would not again smite every living thing as He had done.

easy.question: Which two things would never cease according to verse 22?
answers: Wind and snow
Sea and dry land
Day and night
easy.explanation: The end of the verse says that day and night shall not cease.

medium.question: Why did the Lord decide not to curse the ground again?
answers: Because the imagination of man’s heart is evil from his youth
Because people no longer sin
Because the ground had become holy
medium.explanation: The verse says that the imagination of man’s heart is evil from his youth, so the Lord would not again curse the ground because of man.

medium.question: What does “the imagination of man’s heart” mean in this context?
answers: A good deed
An inner tendency or inclination
A thought about the future
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to an inner tendency or inclination; the context says that human hearts tend toward evil from youth.

medium.question: Which pair describes the agricultural cycle listed in the verse?
answers: Rain and snow
Morning and evening
Seedtime and harvest
medium.explanation: The verse begins with the agricultural cycle of seedtime and harvest, then mentions cold, heat, summer, and winter.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the Lord’s promise not to strike every living thing again?
answers: The world will continue in a natural cycle despite human weakness
All people will now be righteous
There will never be any disasters at all
challenge.explanation: The Lord recognizes human weakness but promises not to destroy every living thing again and preserves the order of nature.

challenge.question: What is significant about the Lord making this promise while saying that man’s heart is evil from his youth?
answers: Humanity has completely changed
The promise is made despite human weakness
Evil has no effect on people
challenge.explanation: The verse does not say that humanity became perfect; instead, it highlights human weakness while the Lord still promises not to destroy every living thing again.

challenge.question: What does the repetition of “I will not again” emphasize in verse 21?
answers: That the Lord will destroy the world gradually
That the promise concerns only the seasons
That the two punishments mentioned will not be repeated
challenge.explanation: The phrase applies to cursing the ground and striking every living thing, emphasizing that the Lord will not repeat those punishments as He had done.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the Lord’s promise not to strike every living thing again?
answers: The world will continue in a natural cycle despite human weakness
All people will now be righteous
There will never be any disasters at all
questions.explanation: The Lord recognizes human weakness but promises not to destroy every living thing again and preserves the order of nature.

questions.question: What is significant about the Lord making this promise while saying that man’s heart is evil from his youth?
answers: Humanity has completely changed
The promise is made despite human weakness
Evil has no effect on people
questions.explanation: The verse does not say that humanity became perfect; instead, it highlights human weakness while the Lord still promises not to destroy every living thing again.

questions.question: What does the repetition of “I will not again” emphasize in verse 21?
answers: That the Lord will destroy the world gradually
That the promise concerns only the seasons
That the two punishments mentioned will not be repeated
questions.explanation: The phrase applies to cursing the ground and striking every living thing, emphasizing that the Lord will not repeat those punishments as He had done.
